name: Stat bars: GTA VI breaks the scale
when: Three figures compared where the last one (GTA VI) is far bigger: bars 1 and 2 land on a shared scale, bar 3 runs to the edge and the scale zooms out to fit it. It sits on a soft, dark shot (see ground).
anchor: Each bar lands on its figure (`at1`, `at2`, `at3`); bar 3 on the GTA VI figure.

vars.theme: clean or vice: the video's theme
vars.title: what is measured (Animations), 24 characters at most
vars.value1: bar 1 figure (decimals are kept as written, up to 2)
vars.label3: bar 3 name, the highlighted one (GTA VI)
vars.value3: bar 3 figure; when it is bigger than bars 1 and 2 it breaks the scale (the scale zooms out to fit it), else it lands like the others
vars.suffix: after bar 3's figure once it has counted up (+); empty = none
vars.source: source line under the chart; empty = none
vars.at1: seconds after the start: when bar 1 starts (its label rises; the bar fills from 4 frames later, over 20 frames, as its figure counts)
vars.at2: seconds after the start: when bar 2 starts (fills over 24 frames)
vars.at3: seconds after the start: when bar 3 starts (fills over 42 frames when it breaks the scale, else 24)
vars.out: seconds after the start: when the chart leaves (the scene ends 0.23 s later)

changed: The scale follows the values: the first two bars set it, and bar 3 breaks it only when it is bigger (with the validated 55,000 / 300,000 / 600,000 the motion is the validated one). The bar fills keep their validated lengths (20, 24 and 42 frames): they are the figures counting with the voice, not an entry, like statbars-B's meters. The soft shot behind the chart is the project's footage, baked from `ground`.
